c.pop: ~740,000 urban (Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture seat; prefecture-wide ~4 million)
c.tagline: China's Grand Canyon, carved through Tujia and Miao mountain country in southwestern Hubei
langs: Tujia and Miao languages (mostly ceremonial/minority use)

card: Credit cards are rarely accepted outside a few international-standard hotels; WeChat Pay and Alipay are used for nearly everything — set up mobile payment before arrival and keep some cash as backup.

taxi.color: mixed liveries, mostly green and white sedans
taxi.fareNote: Meters are standard in town; trips to the Grand Canyon or Tenglong Cave scenic areas are usually flat-rate — agree the price upfront

emergency.note: Fire is 119. English support is minimal — hotel staff can help translate in an emergency.

religion: Folk religion and ancestor veneration (Tujia and Miao traditions)
walk: Downtown Enshi is compact and walkable, but the Grand Canyon, Tenglong Cave and Qingjiang rafting sites are all outside town and require a bus, tour van, or taxi/Didi ride — expect significant stair-climbing and cliffside walkways at the canyon itself.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers; a growing domestic eco-tourism destination with low crime
safety.crime: Minimal — the main risks are trail-related (steep steps, cliffside walkways) rather than crime

hood_landmark.Enshi City Center: Enshi State Central Hospital area and the pedestrian shopping street
hood_landmark.Enshi Railway Station (Jinziba): Enshi Railway Station and its adjacent long-distance coach terminal

hood_desc: The functional prefecture capital with the bus stations, hospitals, and everyday hotels and restaurants — the practical base for exploring the surrounding canyon country.
A dramatic limestone gorge about an hour from downtown, with a glass-floored skywalk and cliffside trails above the Yunlong ground fissure.

The high-speed rail station district about 6 km north of downtown, where most of Enshi's newer chain hotels cluster within walking distance of the station and the long-distance coach terminal across the road; convenient for early trains and for the frequent buses to the Grand Canyon, but a taxi ride from the city's shops and restaurants.
lodging: City Comfort Inn Shizhou Avenue Stadium
Enshi Grand Canyon Yutan Muyun Guesthouse

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as is standard in China.

transit.sys: City buses plus scenic-area shuttle buses
transit.note: Tour buses and shuttles run from downtown to the Grand Canyon and Tenglong Cave; a private driver or Didi is the easiest way to combine multiple sites in a day

transport.air: Enshi Xujiaping Airport (ENH), ~5 km from downtown, with domestic flights to Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Xi'an and other major cities
transport.train: Enshi railway station on the Yichang-Wanzhou line connects to Wuhan (~4-5 hrs) and Chongqing
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect Enshi to Wuhan, Chongqing, and Zhangjiajie; local buses and scenic shuttles serve the canyon and cave
transport.ferry: None — Enshi is inland mountain terrain with no scheduled passenger ferry service
transport.car: Self-driving or a hired driver is useful for combining the Grand Canyon, Tenglong Cave, and Yumu Village in one trip; mountain roads are winding but well paved to the main sites

airport.name: Enshi Xujiaping Airport
airport.transport: Airport shuttle bus to the city center; taxi/Didi also available

net.m: Good 4G in downtown Enshi and along main roads; patchy inside the canyon and cave scenic areas
net.w: Free wifi in most hotels and cafes
net.ops: China Mobile, China Unicom, China Telecom
net.gb: ~$3-5 per GB on a prepaid tourist SIM
net.fwn: The Great Firewall blocks Google, WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook — install a VPN before arrival
net.ap: Buy a SIM or eSIM in Wuhan or another major hub before traveling to Enshi; local stock is limited

tip.s: Not expected — tipping isn't part of Chinese service culture
tip.r: No tipping at restaurants; rarely a service charge outside upscale hotel restaurants

food.name: Zhaguangjiao
food.desc: Enshi's defining Tujia preserve: red chillies pounded with cornmeal and fermented in a jar, then pan-fried until crisp or stir-fried with pork and potato.

places.name: Ba Ren Tang
places.note: Theatrical Tujia restaurant on Daughter Street built around local staples and bowl-smashing wine.

places.name: Aoshan Folk Custom Street
places.note: Row of Tujia restaurants with nightly song and dance; reliable for the classic chilli-and-corn dishes.

places.name: Wuyangba food streets
places.note: Dozens of everyday local kitchens where zhaguangjiao comes fried with pork belly.

food.name: Hezha
food.desc: Lazy tofu: soybeans ground with their pulp and simmered with chopped greens into a soft, savoury mash, the everyday Tujia comfort dish.

places.name: Zhangguan Hezha restaurants
places.note: The best-known name for hezha, cooked dry then finished with pork, chicken and fresh stock.

places.name: Ba Ren Tang
places.note: Serves hezha as part of a full Tujia spread with smoked meat and corn rice.

places.name: Liujiaoting old town eateries
places.note: Small neighbourhood kitchens in the old quarter doing the plain home-style version.

food.name: La rou (Tujia cured pork)
food.desc: Pork salted then hung over a smoky kitchen fire for months, sliced thin and stir-fried with garlic shoots, dried radish or wild bamboo shoots.

places.name: Ba Ren Tang
places.note: Cured meats are the house speciality, served with corn wine in a Tujia-themed hall.

places.name: Aoshan Folk Custom Street
places.note: Hanging-pot restaurants here build their pots around home-smoked bacon and sausage.

places.name: Enshi city farmers markets
places.note: Village smokers sell whole cured legs and sausage; stalls will vacuum-pack for travel.

food.name: Diaoguo (Tujia hanging pot)
food.desc: A cast-iron pot hung over a wood fire in the middle of the table, filled with cured pork, potatoes, tofu and greens and eaten communally all evening.

places.name: Aoshan Folk Custom Street
places.note: The city's signature hanging-pot banquet with opera and bowl-smashing wine from 7pm.

places.name: Ba Ren Tang
places.note: Hanging pots served in a Tujia cultural setting; popular with groups, book at weekends.

places.name: Restaurants near Enshi Grand Canyon
places.note: Village restaurants on the canyon road do wood-fired pots with mountain vegetables.

food.name: Baogufan and kang tudou
food.desc: Cornmeal steamed through rice into golden baogufan, served with kang tudou, small mountain potatoes fried whole with chilli, salt and wild pepper.

places.name: Wuyangba food streets
places.note: Potato stalls fry them to order all evening; the cheapest and best street snack in Enshi.

places.name: Liujiaoting old town eateries
places.note: Old-quarter kitchens still serve corn rice as the default staple with soup and pickles.

places.name: Nuer Cheng night market
places.note: Rows of griddles doing small potatoes and grilled tofu after dark.

food.name: Enshi yulu tea
food.desc: China's rare surviving steamed green tea, needle-straight and grassy-sweet; grown on the misty selenium-rich slopes around Enshi.

places.name: Enshi Yulu tea houses
places.note: Dedicated tea rooms brew the local leaf properly and sell it by the tin.

places.name: Nuer Cheng tea shops
places.note: Tourist-facing but genuine tastings of yulu and selenium teas from nearby villages.

places.name: Enshi city farmers markets
places.note: Growers sell loose spring-picked yulu at far lower prices than gift-boxed tins.

food.name: Baogu jiu (corn wine)
food.desc: Cloudy home-distilled corn liquor and sweeter fermented rice wine, poured for guests in coarse bowls that are smashed after the toast.

places.name: Ba Ren Tang
places.note: Runs the Tujia bowl-smashing wine ritual nightly as part of the meal.

places.name: Aoshan Folk Custom Street
places.note: Corn wine comes with the hanging-pot banquet and the evening performance.

places.name: Village guesthouses, Enshi Grand Canyon
places.note: Family-run stays pour their own corn spirit; the most honest version you will find.

landmarks: Enshi Grand Canyon
A spectacular karst gorge of sheer cliffs and cloud-wrapped pinnacles, crowned by the impossibly slender One Incense Pillar rock column.
Tenglong Cave
One of the world's largest cave systems near Lichuan, its cathedral-sized entrance swallowing a whole river before a light-show-filled subterranean walk.
Enshi Tusi City
A sprawling recreation of a Tujia chieftain's walled capital, where wooden stilt towers, ceremonial gates and the Nine-Level Hall climb a hillside.
Qingjiang River Cruise (Butterfly Cliff)
A serene boat journey through emerald karst canyons of the Qingjiang, passing the vast butterfly-shaped rock face that symbolizes the river.
Suobuya Stone Forest
A labyrinth of gray karst pinnacles and mossy gullies dubbed the world's oldest stone forest, threaded with walkways and Tujia legends.
Shiziguan Floating Bridge
A photogenic pontoon boardwalk snaking across a jade-green gorge lake, made famous by drone videos of cars gliding over the water.
Pingshan Canyon
A narrow crystal-clear gorge near Hefeng where flat-bottomed boats appear to float on air above transparent green water.
Enshi Girl City (Nü'er Cheng)
A lively Tujia-themed town celebrating the region's matchmaking festival traditions with nightly folk shows, snack streets and stilted architecture.
Qingjiang Wind-Rain Bridge
An ornate covered pedestrian bridge in traditional Dong-Tujia style spanning the Qingjiang in central Enshi, glowing lantern-red after dark.
Yumu Village (Yumuzhai)
A fortress-like Tujia village atop sheer cliffs, reached by ancient stone paths and ringed by terraced fields and hanging plank roads.

train.note: Enshi has no international trains. Enshi Railway Station on Jingui Boulevard sits on the Yichang-Wanzhou line, which cuts through the mountains of western Hubei with direct services to Wuhan, Chongqing, Chengdu, Beijing and Shanghai. City bus lines 6, 11 and 22 and tour bus 4 connect the station with the centre. Book on 12306 with your passport; the line is single-tracked in places and heavily used, so seats towards Wuhan and Chongqing sell out early in the holiday peaks.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Enshi. Enshi Hangkong Road Bus Station, opposite the railway station, is the main long-distance terminal and runs frequent services out of the province as well as to Yichang and Wuhan, while the Lichuan South Gate terminal covers short local routes to the scenic areas around Lichuan and the surrounding counties. Tickets are sold at the counters; buses are still the only way to reach the Enshi Grand Canyon and the Tenglong Cave.

ferry.note: Enshi is deep in the mountains of western Hubei and has no scheduled passenger ferries. The only boats are sightseeing craft on the Qingjiang River gorges and inside the show caves, sold as part of the scenic-area tickets.

half.name: Lichuan & Dashuijing Ancient Architecture Complex
half.blurb: Qing-dynasty clan compound of stone gate towers and courtyard houses near Lichuan, about an hour from Enshi.

full.name: Shennong Stream
full.blurb: Narrow tributary canyon of the Yangtze near Badong, toured by traditional wooden pea-boats between towering limestone cliffs.
